title: Three-sided Ambush
next_chapter_hook: Winds howled beneath the cliff. Chen Ji gazed up at that wildly laughing figure, a cold smile curling at the corner of his lips—Han Lie, you think you've won, but you'll never know that the 'dead man' you just let go with your own hands will show you what true despair means at the moment of your greatest triumph.

text.content: The sound of the teacup shattering was especially jarring in the quiet bamboo hut. Chen Ji lowered his gaze to the tea stains on his palm, something churning in the depths of his eyes. That piece he had never calculated—what could it be? The movements of the Holy Sect? Or... the gaze of Heaven? He raced through possibilities in his mind, yet his expression remained the numb facade thattrash disciples always wore. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul in the Tianji Record's first page rippled faintly, seemingly awaiting his decision.

Yet time waits for no one. The forces of the three major sects had already set out. His intelligence network had caught wind of movements from Xuanwu Sect and Qingming Sect scouts—all converging toward the same location. Chen Ji took a deep breath, suppressing the unease. No matter what pieces had been added to the board, the game could no longer be halted. He rose slowly, the hunched posture of thetrash disciple vanishing, replaced by the composed stance of a predator lying in wait.

dialogue.content:
"Since you wish to come, then come.
He murmured to himself, a cold smile playing at his lips. From his sleeve he produced three jade slips prepared long ago, sealing within them tokens marked with different sect insignia. These pieces of intelligence seemed random, but were meticulously calculated—each pointed to the same location, yet could be verified independently, making the recipient believe they possessed exclusive information. Using others as blades—this was a game he played better than anyone.

text.content: He handed the three jade slips to his hidden agents lying in ambush, movements fluid and without hesitation. Then Chen Ji began meticulously preparing his 'death' performance—he applied specially made blood packets to the inside of his outer garment. These packets, when struck with force, would burst with bloodstains convincing enough to fool anyone. He even placed a fragile fake pulse patch at his neck, making the 'tragic scene' of falling from the cliff even more heart-wrenching.

choice.prompt: When Chen Ji conducted his final inspection of the trap arrangement, he discovered a subtle variable—the forces of the demonic path Holy Sect were also moving toward the same location. Should he ignore this variable and proceed with the original plan, or adjust his strategy on the fly?

choices.description: Ye Qing's demonic path miasma can conceal the Tianji Record's aura. Her people appearing on site would instead increase the chaos, making the mutual constraining effect among multiple forces better.
choices.risk_hint: If Ye Qing turns traitor at the last moment or is exploited by other forces, it could lead to total defeat.

text.content: Chen Ji decided to incorporate Ye Qing's forces into his chess game. Although the demonic path experts under her command came from questionable origins, in such a chaotic multi-party battle, they would serve as the best disruptive pieces. Through the Tianji Record Fragment, he transmitted a vague prophecy to Ye Qing, hinting that if she wished the Holy Sect to pay a price, she should not miss this grand gathering.

choices.text: Adjust Plan to Avoid Demonic Path
choices.description: The demonic path forces posed too great a variable. Chen Ji decided to temporarily modify the intelligence content, causing the demonic path forces to miss this spectacle and reducing uncontrollable risks.
choices.risk_hint: Modifying the intelligence would require time, possibly missing the optimal timing, and could raise Ye Qing's suspicions.

text.content: Chen Ji decisively modified part of the intelligence content, making hidden adjustments to the routes demonic path forces might take. He believed Ye Qing's intelligence would lead her to the correct judgment—even if her people failed to witness this grand spectacle firsthand, she would understand it was to protect mutual cooperation.

Three days later, at dusk. Sunset Peak. Chen Ji stood alone atop a massive boulder at the peak, the hunched silhouette of thetrash disciple casting a long shadow in the evening sun. His expression remained as cowardly as ever, as if the one about to face death was merely a lamb awaiting slaughter. Yet his spiritual sense had already spread wide, perceiving the killing intent flooding in from all directions—the fierce blade aura of Xuanwu Sect, the阴柔 sword qi of Qingming Sect, the肃杀 murderous aura of the Imperial Court, and... that faint demonic path miasma.

"They're here.
Chen Ji counted silently in his heart. The first was Xuanwu Sect's blade light—the attacker with狂暴而 direct aura, precisely a disciple under Han Lie as he had anticipated. The second was Qingming Sect's hidden weapons, the whooshing sound subtle yet deadly. The third was the Imperial Court's Brocade Guards, few in number but perfectly coordinated. The fourth... was the demonic path forces. Ye Qing had indeed not let him down. Five factions, five directions, converging toward the peak where he stood in an exquisite rhythm.

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji! Today is your death!" Han Lie's voice exploded first, his霸道 steps thundering up to the peak, his blade carving burning blade light through the air. His eyes blazed with long-suppressed fury—thistrash actually dared time and again to humiliate him. Today he would personally tear him to pieces!

text.content: Chen Ji's lips twitched slightly—not from fear, but because Han Lie's flamboyant posturing was simply too laughable. It was as if he could already see what would happen next: all factions would strike simultaneously, then discover each other's presence, and the 'assassination of Chen Ji' would transform into 'mutual restraint.' And he? He only needed to play his part in this 'tragic death' scene. The reputation oftrash Chen Ji would end here—at least in the eyes of the world.

choice.prompt: Han Lie swung his blade, the sword path fierce enough to seem like it would cleave the very air in two. Facing an attack that could instantly kill an ordinary Foundation Building disciple, how should Chen Ji respond?

choices.description: "He deliberately dispersed his protective spiritual energy as the blade qi approached, allowing the blade light to tear through his outer clothing and carve a shallow bloodstain on his chest, 'screaming in agony' as he stumbled backward. This scene had to be sufficiently realistic to make everyone present believe he was severely wounded and on the verge of death."
choices.risk_hint: "If the blade qi isn't controlled properly, he could truly suffer serious injuries or even death"

text.content: "The blade light tore through his outer clothing, leaving a bloodstain on his chest. Chen Ji let out a闷哼, 'terrified' as he retreated several steps, his foot caught on something, and his entire body toppled toward the cliff edge. His performance was impeccable—his face twisted with 'pain' even carried an expression of disbelief, as if he couldn't believe until death that Han Lie actually dared to make a move."

choices.description: "Consume 5 points of Heavenly Fate, using the Tianji Record's foresight ability to 'see' the trajectories of all attacks within the next three breaths, precisely controlling his timing of 'pitiful death'—acting convincingly enough without actually suffering serious injuries."
choices.risk_hint: "After consuming Heavenly Fate, it may affect the fault tolerance rate of subsequent plans"

text.content: "The Tianji Record's fragment unfolded a clear vision of the future in his mind. Chen Ji saw that four attacks would come simultaneously in the next moment—he only needed to 'accidentally' get hit by one of them at the last instant, then顺势fall from the cliff. He perfectly controlled his body, floundering left and right amid the blade light and swords, each 'failed dodge'恰到好处—neither too fake nor actually injured."

"Just then, a sudden change occurred.\n\nThe second attack, third attack, fourth attack descended almost simultaneously—the hidden weapons from Qingming Sect, the crossbow bolts from Imperial Dynasty's Brocade Guards, and the black mist from the demonic path experts. Assassins from five factions discovered each other's presence almost simultaneously, and the assassination moves originally targeting Chen Ji instantly became the opening of a chaotic battle. The clash of blades, the whistling of hidden weapons piercing the air, and the intertwined shouts and grunts—the entire mountaintop instantly turned into a修罗场."

"And Chen Ji, taking advantage of this brief chaos, 'stumbled' toward the cliff edge.\n\nHis performance was seamless—every step filled with despair and struggle, every stumble perfectly displaying the fear and helplessness of atrash disciple facing death. The bloodstain on his chest was especially glaring under the setting sun, matching his pale complexion and trembling hands—anyone seeing this would believe this was a dying man about to fall off the cliff."

dialogue.content: "He's running!\n\nHan Lie roared, his blade momentum suddenly surging, actually abandoning the enemy before him and径直chasing after Chen Ji. His reason had long been burned away by rage, with only one thought in his mind—thistrash must die by his hand! However, just as his blade light was about to touch Chen Ji's back, a black figure suddenly burst from the side, black mist swirling in its hand, forcefully intercepting his blade momentum."

text.content: "Chen Ji felt that狂暴murderous intent behind him, and a barely perceptible arc curled at the corner of his mouth.\n\nHan Lie, you think you're chasing me, but you're actually helping me complete my final curtain call. He seemed to slip, his entire body tilting toward the cliff edge. In that instant, he spread his arms wide, making a posture of embracing the void—like a折翼bird falling from the cliff's edge. The blood packet on his chest exploded at the same moment, crimson blood blooming into a shocking flower in the air."

choice.prompt: "In the moment of falling from the cliff, Chen Ji saw Han Lie rush to the cliff edge, his face full of disbelief. Should he let him continue in his misunderstanding, or give him a 'surprise' at this final moment?"

choices.text: "Stay Silent, Disappear into the Sea of Clouds"
choices.description: "Thetrash disciple Chen Ji is already dead—from now on he will walk the world with another identity. Han Lie will never know the truth, and this 'permanent misunderstanding' is the most perfect revenge."
choices.visible_reward: "Maximum Effect of Feigning Weakness to Strike Back"
choices.risk_hint: "Han Lie may become even more arrogant because of this, possibly becoming a hidden danger in the future"

text.content: "Chen Ji let the clouds and mist swallow his figure, the mocking arc at the corner of his mouth disappearing into the wind. In the final moment of falling, he heard Han Lie's near-lunatic laughter from the cliff top—that laughter was full of the satisfaction of revenge achieved, not knowing this 'dead man' would, at the most unexpected moment, give him an unforgettable surprise."

choices.description: "In the instant he fell into the sea of clouds, Chen Ji said something with only Han Lie could hear—a sentence that would make him restless for the rest of his life. True revenge isn't letting him die, but making him live to endure endless torment."
choices.visible_reward: A fatal blow to the spirit
choices.risk_hint: If Han Lie senses something amiss, he might take precautions

dialogue.content:
Han Lie, do you think this is the end?

Chen Ji's voice drifted away with the wind, as light as an illusion, yet it clearly pierced into Han Lie's ears. The words were like a poisoned thorn, deeply embedded in his heart. From now on, every time he thought he had won, he would remember these words, remember the eerie smile on thattrash's face as he fell from the cliff.

text.content:
The battle at the cliff's summit persisted, but Han Lie was now too distracted to care.

He stood frozen at the cliff's edge, gazing at the churning sea of clouds, the words echoing endlessly in his mind. The thrill of revenge had vanished, replaced by an inexplicable chill. Thattrash... was he truly dead? Why did Han Lie feel something was fundamentally wrong? Why did those dying words unsettle him so profoundly? Han Lie gripped his long blade tightly, knuckles whitening with tension. He told himself those were merely the ramblings of a dying wretch, yet the lingering shadow in his heart refused to dissipate.

Meanwhile, in a secluded mountain cave beneath the cliff, Chen Ji was calmly brushing dust from his robes.

Not a single scratch marked his body. The blood trail on his chest came from a pre-prepared blood pack, and the weightlessness during the fall was merely thanks to a pre-positioned buffer formation. Those people thought he was dead, but he was very much alive—more alive than ever before. Thetrash disciple Chen Ji had been buried, and a new identity, a new chess game, awaited him. Chen Ji lifted his head, gazing toward the cliff summit through the cave entrance, a meaningful smile curving his lips.

It's just... whose chess piece was this, never factored into his calculations?

This question festered in his heart like a thorn. The Tianji Record Fragment pulsed warmly in his mind, seemingly reminding him of something. Chen Ji closed his eyes, beginning to recalculate this game that had been in play for over a decade. Every move, every piece, every variable—he calculated swiftly within his mind. Yet that chess piece's outline remained frustratingly blurred, as if dwelling in a dimension beyond his reach. Master Mo's lingering soul sighed softly from the first page of the Tianji Record, the sigh carrying some profound significance.

Forget it—cross that bridge when we come to it.

Chen Ji opened his eyes, the numb expression typical oftrash disciples resettling onto his face. He slowly walked out of the mountain cave, stepping into the night. The chaotic battle at Sunset Peak should now be spreading throughout the entire cultivation world—thetrash disciple Chen Ji, pursued by Xuanwu Sect's Han Lie, had fallen from a cliff to his death. What a perfect obituary, what a reasonable ending. From now on, there would be no moretrash Chen Ji in this world—only a new piece lurking in the shadows, gazing down at the chessboard. And those who considered themselves chess players would never know that the true game had just begun.

Wind howled beneath the cliff as Chen Ji gazed at the figure laughing wildly above, a cold smile forming at the corner of his lips—Han Lie, you think you've won, but you'll never know that the 'dead man' you just personally released will show you what despair means at the moment of your greatest triumph. And more importantly, that chess piece he could never calculate has quietly landed at the edge of his new chessboard, waiting for its moment to enter in a way utterly beyond his prediction.
